question: In a skewed smooth distribution with a tail exended to the left, the statistic with the highest value is the
options: median
interquartile range
geometric mean
quartile deviation
variance
range
standard deviation
mean
mode
harmonic mean
model_outputs: A skewed smooth distribution with a tail extended to the left is negatively skewed, meaning the majority of the data is on the right side of the mean, and the left tail is longer. In such a distribution, the mean (H) is pulled to the right by the larger values, while the median (A) is less affected by the skewness and lies closer to the center of the distribution. The mode (I) is the most common value, but in a negatively skewed distribution, it may not be the highest value. The geometric mean (C) and harmonic mean (J) are not affected by outliers and are also not typically used for skewed distributions. The interquartile range (B), quartile deviation (D), range (F), variance (E), and standard deviation (G) are all measures that are influenced by the outliers and skewed distribution, making the mean the highest value in this case. The answer is (H).
